issues.description: The problem statement (UML) declares a Pneumatic interface with methods raisePressure(int) and openValve(), but the solution's Pneumatic interface declares raisePressure(int) and releaseValve(). Furthermore, the solution's implementing classes (LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster) implement openValve(), causing a mismatch between the interface and implementations. This discrepancy is structural and will prevent successful compilation and confuses students about the required method name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Pneumatic interface match the UML and the implementing classes by declaring void openValve() (replace releaseValve() with openValve()), or alternatively rename the implementations to releaseValve() and update the UML/problem text accordingly. Ensure the interface and all implementing classes use the same method name.

issues.description: The UML/problem statement defines a Pneumatic interface with methods raisePressure(...) and openValve(). In the solution, the Pneumatic interface declares raisePressure(...) and releaseValve(), while the implementing classes (LaunchedRollerCoaster and LaunchedDropdownTower) override openValve(). This inconsistent naming (openValve vs. releaseValve) represents the same conceptual operation but uses different identifiers across artifacts, causing a confusing mapping for students and likely leading to compilation/test mismatches.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across all artifacts. Either rename releaseValve() in src/de/tum/in/ase/Pneumatic.java to openValve(), or update the UML/problem statement to use releaseValve() and change the implementing classes to override releaseValve(). Prefer changing the Pneumatic interface in the solution to declare openValve() to match the UML/problem statement and the implementing classes.
